alerts.title: Weight gain likely from uncontrolled hypothyroidism, not DTG
alerts.message: The clinician attributes the patient's 9 kg weight gain to DTG and is considering switching away from DTG. However, the patient has classic hypothyroidism signs (tiredness, cold intolerance, constipation, dry skin, periorbital puffiness, delayed reflexes) with TSH 12.4 mIU/L and low Free T4. She reports often forgetting her levothyroxine. Untreated hypothyroidism is a well-recognized cause of significant weight gain and could fully account for the 9 kg increase. Switching from DTG without first correcting the hypothyroidism may not resolve the weight issue and risks losing the benefits of a well-tolerated, high-genetic-barrier regimen with viral suppression.

evidence.recommended_action: Optimise levothyroxine adherence and dose to normalise TSH before attributing weight gain to DTG or switching ART. Reassess weight after thyroid control is achieved.

alerts.title: DTG hyperglycaemia risk: multiple risk factors present
alerts.message: Guidelines require screening for hyperglycaemia risk factors before initiating or transitioning to DTG, with fasting glucose checked if 2 or more risk factors are present (age ≥30, BMI ≥25, family history of DM, history of hypertension). This patient has at least two risk factors: age 45 and BMI 33. Today's fasting glucose is 5.6 mmol/L, which is in the impaired fasting glucose range. Guidelines also recommend monitoring blood glucose every 3 months for high-risk patients in the first 12 months. No ongoing glucose monitoring plan is documented.

evidence.recommended_action: Counsel patient on diet and lifestyle. Repeat fasting glucose at next visit and consider HbA1c given impaired fasting glucose and multiple risk factors.

alerts.title: Elevated lipids not addressed in clinician plan
alerts.message: The patient has LDL 4.2 mmol/L, total cholesterol 6.4 mmol/L, and triglycerides 2.3 mmol/L, all elevated. She is on TDF/3TC/DTG; DTG is generally lipid-neutral, so the dyslipidemia may reflect metabolic syndrome compounded by hypothyroidism and obesity (BMI 33). The clinician's plan does not address the abnormal lipid panel. Untreated dyslipidemia in an overweight patient increases cardiovascular risk. Hypothyroidism itself can worsen lipid abnormalities and should be corrected before attributing the pattern to ART alone.

evidence.recommended_action: Address hypothyroidism, counsel on diet and exercise, and recheck lipid panel after TSH normalisation. Consider cardiovascular risk assessment.

alerts.title: TDF renal monitoring overdue by 6 months
alerts.message: Guidelines require serum creatinine and eGFR monitoring for patients on TDF-based regimens. The most recent creatinine is from August 2025 (196 days ago) and no eGFR is documented. TDF can cause chronic kidney disease, acute kidney injury, and Fanconi syndrome. While the last creatinine of 72 umol/L was normal, no renal monitoring has been performed in over 6 months and none is planned today. The patient also has hypothyroidism, which can affect renal function.

evidence.recommended_action: Check serum creatinine and eGFR today and ensure regular renal monitoring is scheduled per TDF guidelines.
